subject: Post-call: model fit roadmap, snapshot hold & rollback trigger criteria
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily@harborpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: model fit roadmap, snapshot hold & rollback trigger criteria

Hi Emily — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope and risk controls: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use: customer support triage + automated reply suggestions for payments disputes (~60% short-form replies).
- Success metrics: top-1 relevance on golden set >= 88%, false-positive rate on escalation < 5%.
- Latency target: p95 generation < 450ms for 512-token window.

Recommended immediate artifacts (attached):
- eval_benchmarks_20260514.csv — initial golden-set scores across candidates (we ran Redwood-XL, Redwood-Quant-8, and OpenModel-Base).
- prompt_set_v1.jsonl — representative prompts we suggest for your smoke tests.
- mutual_action_plan.pdf — proposed timeline and responsibilities.

Risk note (important): During our internal rerun this morning one of the candidate variants (Redwood-XL v2.1) showed a 4.5 point drop on the golden set vs. v2.0 on short-form urgency detection. Given your tolerance, we recommend placing a snapshot hold on any rollout and pinning production traffic to v2.0 until we:
  1) run your golden-set smoke tests (2–4 hours)
  2) run an expanded regression sweep (24 hours)
  3) decide on rollback/pinning based on preset thresholds below.

Rollback / pin triggers (proposed):
- If top-1 golden-set accuracy drops > 2.0 absolute points OR
- If escalation false-positive increases > 2.0 percentage points OR
- If customer-facing complaint rate within first 24h > 1% of transactions

Proposed next steps:
1) You run the attached prompt_set_v1 against the three model candidates we shared and drop results into the Drive link — we’ll stand by to help.
2) We will freeze any automatic upgrade paths in your Dedicated environment (pinning to v2.0) until we mutually clear v2.1.
3) On green, we’ll schedule a canary rollout with traffic siphoning and trace hooks.

If that sounds OK I’ll raise the snapshot request and pin the model on your Dedicated project.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit roadmap, snapshot hold & rollback trigger criteria

Thanks, Dylan — this is exactly what we need. A couple of clarifying points from our side before we run the smoke tests: 

- Can you call out which exact metric in the CSV corresponds to the "urgency detection" slice? I want to make sure our engineers map the right score.
- If we pin to v2.0, is there any manual step our infra team must take, or can you enforce that from Redwood Dedicated?

We'll start running prompt_set_v1 this afternoon (ETA: results in the Drive by EOD). If we see the same gap you observed, we'd prefer an immediate temporary pin while we triage — please confirm your rollback latency (how quickly you can revert traffic to v2.0).

—Emily
Emily Chen

emily@harborpay.com | +1 617-555-2102
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-14T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit roadmap, snapshot hold & rollback trigger criteria

Looping in technical ops context — re: rollback latency and enforcement:

- We can enforce pinning from the Redwood control plane immediately for Dedicated projects; that toggles routing rules and stops any automated model promotions. Enforcement is effectively instant (within our internal orchestration window), but traffic routing convergence ~ 2–5 minutes depending on active connections.
- For the regression numbers: the urgency slice in the CSV is column "urgency_f1_short" (we computed micro-F1 over annotated short-form intents). The 4.5-point drop is on that metric comparing XL v2.1 -> v2.0.
- Quick ask: Rishi, please upload the per-prompt diffs and the token-level trace for three failing examples to the Drive folder so we can triage parity vs. prompt sensitivity.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-14T18:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit roadmap, snapshot hold & rollback trigger criteria

On it — I ran the failing prompts through a debug harness and attached short diffs in the Drive. Short summary:
- Two prompts show beam-level re-ranking differences (v2.1 favors a more verbose acknowledgement causing score drop).
- One prompt shows truncation interplay with the new attention-kernel (edge case at token 512).
- Quick mitigation options:
  * Pin to v2.0 (fast, eliminates regression risk immediately)
  * Apply a prompt-normalization shim (medium effort; lower risk of behavior changes)
  * Patch the runtime kernel and re-evaluate (higher effort; longer lead time)

I recommend we pin v2.0 for the short window while we run the full regression suite overnight including HarborPay's prompt_set_v1. I'll prepare the regression report (CSV + three annotated examples) within 6–8 hours.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Staff ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily@harborpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-15T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit roadmap, snapshot hold & rollback trigger criteria

Emily — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on Rishi's findings and your preference for stability, here's the recommended immediate plan: 

1) We will execute an enforced pin to Redwood-XL v2.0 on your Dedicated project at 11:45 PT today. This is a control-plane action on our side — no infra steps required from HarborPay. 
2) We will run the overnight regression suite (Redwood + HarborPay prompt_set_v1). Expect full report in the Drive by 08:00 PT tomorrow; includes CSV, per-prompt diffs, and token traces. 
3) Decision ladder after the regression: 
   - If golden-set drop <= 1.0 point and no escalation deltas > 1.0%: proceed to staged canary for v2.1 with tracing.
   - Else: maintain v2.0 pin and open a runbook with the runtime team to prioritize kernel fixes.

If you approve, I’ll schedule the pin and send a notification once it’s in effect. Also attaching the mutual_action_plan.pdf with timelines and owners.

Quick ask: can HarborPay engineering confirm a point-of-contact for the overnight logs? We’ll need someone to confirm acceptance of the regression CSV once uploaded.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.ai
